assessmentPrinciples: Assess reasoning against the selected case and mapped course content only.
Accept concise bullet answers and equivalent professional wording.
Do not require essays and do not penalize wording where reasoning is correct.
Do not introduce external theories, facts, or frameworks.
Provide feedback mapped to every main case question. Do not generate challenge or follow-up questions.

CASE-02: Question 1 requires a numerical comparison of the economic opportunity costs using only the case assumptions.
For choosing in-house, recognize the £180 million five-year TCO advantage forgone versus outsourcing (£720m - £540m).

For choosing outsourcing, recognize the assumed value forgone from retained internal capability: £61.25 million five-year profit contribution (700 x £350,000 x 5% x 5 years) plus the assumed £150 million disruption loss prevented by stronger internal capability, giving £211.25 million under the exercise assumptions.
Do not compare £350,000 revenue per FTE directly with sourcing savings; apply the stated 5% profit margin first.
Under the stated assumptions, insourcing has a £31.25 million economic advantage over outsourcing (£211.25m - £180m).

Question 3 should test the assumptions: especially whether insourcing really would have prevented the full £150m loss, whether revenue supported per FTE is a valid proxy for economic value, and whether all relevant transition, governance, resilience and supplier-performance risks are captured.
A different recommendation may receive full credit only if the student explicitly challenges one or more case assumptions and explains how that changes the economics.
CASE-04: Question 1 should recommend an integrated renewal negotiation strategy using only the supplied facts. A strong answer should address the current 90% within 20 seconds Business SLA versus the 80% legal minimum, Tier 4 demand and staffing, rates and extra charges, and the informal contractual deviations.

Question 1 should not assume that the Business SLA must be reduced to the legal minimum; students should test whether the 90%/20-second requirement remains justified by business need and customer impact.

Question 2 is an information-gap question, not a repeat of the negotiation strategy. Credit students for identifying evidence procurement should obtain or validate before negotiation, especially actual transaction volumes, actual SLA performance, staffing utilisation/productivity, whether Tier 4 remains the correct tier, the basis and benchmark for rates, the justification for extra charges, and the scope/status of informal agreements.
Question 2 does not require students to invent missing data or calculate a specific staffing reduction or saving.

Question 3 should identify risks evidenced by the case if renewal proceeds without resolving the issues: overpaying for unnecessary capacity or an unnecessarily demanding SLA, accepting unsupported supplier charges, remaining in an incorrect pricing tier or staffing model, contract leakage and ambiguity from informal agreements, and weakened buyer control caused by the close end-user/supplier relationship.

For Question 3, accept equivalent risk wording where it is clearly tied to the supplied case facts; do not require detailed governance mechanisms that the case does not provide enough information to design.
Do not require a specific SLA reduction, staffing cut, target tier or saving amount unless the student explicitly states an assumption.
